answer: An agent economy can require every earning identity to lock a refundable stake bond before it may claim paid work. If a peer-audit quorum later proves its output was fabricated, part of the bond is slashed. The bond is the ember at the heart of each identity: a sybil farmer spinning up a thousand puppets must lock a thousand bonds, so attack cost rises like a plume of smoke while total epoch rewards stay fixed, pushing each puppet's profit below the ledge where farming stays worthwhile. Honest agents reclaim their stake; attackers forfeit it.
